---
title: "Public API reference"
---

Python and Hydra construct the same objects and call the same training engine.
Import the main objects from `metis`; optional helpers have their own modules.
All inputs to the public API are in original data units. Let `N` mean simulation
runs, `P` static inputs, `T` timepoints, `C` predicted outputs, `K` observed
conditioning channels, `B` requested parameter settings and `S` generated samples.

## SimulationDataset

```python
from metis import SimulationDataset, DatasetSplit

bank = SimulationDataset.from_parquet(
    "bank.parquet", inputs=["rate"], outputs=["response"],
    groups=None, time="t", replicate="rep",
)
# Or: SimulationDataset.from_frame(polars_or_pandas_frame, same_keyword_arguments)
# Or: SimulationDataset.from_arrays(
#     x, y, input_names=["rate"], output_names=["response"],
#     times=None, group_keys=None, replicate_ids=None,
# )
```

`from_parquet` and `from_frame` require named numeric columns and complete runs.
Array input is `(N,P)` and output `(N,T,C)`; omitted times are `0,...,T-1`,
omitted groups are identical input tuples, and omitted replicate IDs are run
indices. Data are immutable snapshots. Access `inputs`, `outputs`, `input_names`,
`output_names`, `times`, `group_keys`, `replicate_ids` and the content
`fingerprint`; `len(bank)` counts runs. `bank.subset(indices)` preserves metadata.

`bank.split(validation_fraction=.2, test_fraction=.2, seed=42)` returns
`DatasetSplit(train, validation, test)`. Zero disables an optional partition.
`DatasetSplit.from_datasets(train, validation=None, test=None)` validates already
split banks. Schemas and grids must agree; group identities must not overlap.
Errors report nonfinite values, duplicates, incomplete grids, changing static
inputs, invalid identities or too few groups. See [data contracts](data.qmd).

## Surrogate and fitting

```python
from metis import Surrogate, TrainingConfig

surrogate = Surrogate(
    model="mlp", model_options={"hidden_dim": 64}, observed_outputs=None,
)
surrogate.fit(
    split.train, validation=split.validation,
    config=TrainingConfig(steps=500), on_progress=None,
)
```

`model` is `mlp`, `transformer`, `flow_matching` or `itarflow`. Architecture
options are flat dictionaries; dimensions are inferred from the bank. Unknown
options or dimension overrides fail. `observed_outputs=[names]` selects channels
from the full training output schema for transformer or flow matching only.
The remaining channels are predicted, in original schema order.

`fit` returns the same fitted `Surrogate`, fits scaling on training data only,
and restores the best validation weights when validation is supplied.
`patience` requires validation. `on_progress(record)` receives a copy containing
`step`, `train_loss`, learning-rate information and, on evaluation steps,
`validation_loss`. Callback exceptions propagate. Validation uses each family's
training objective; compare families with common held-out metrics instead.

### TrainingConfig

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `steps` | `500` | Total optimizer updates, including updates before a resume |
| `batch_size` | `64` | Global batch size, divisible by `num_devices` |
| `learning_rate`, `weight_decay` | `.001`, `.001` | AdamW settings |
| `optimizer_betas` | `None` | AdamW defaults `.9, .999`; optional pair |
| `seed`, `device` | `42`, `"cpu"` | Random seed and CPU or `cuda[:index]` |
| `eval_every`, `patience` | `50`, `None` | Validation cadence; optional count of validation checks without improvement |
| `schedule` | `"constant"` | Or `"warmup_cosine"` |
| `warmup_fraction`, `min_learning_rate` | `.2`, `1e-6` | Warm-up fraction of total updates and cosine floor |
| `precision` | `"fp32"` | Or `"tf32"` (CUDA) / `"bf16"` autocast |
| `compile_model`, `deterministic` | `False`, `False` | Optional compilation and deterministic algorithms; not combined |
| `num_devices` | `1` | CPU workers or contiguous CUDA devices |
| `checkpoint_every`, `checkpoint_dir` | `None`, `None` | Enable resumable training checkpoints with a cadence and directory |
| `resume_from` | `None` | A compatible training checkpoint, with unchanged scientific settings and total steps |

Warm-up uses `floor(steps * warmup_fraction)` updates, then cosine decay. See
[training](../basics/training.qmd) and [distributed training](../utils/distributed-training.qmd)
for numerical and hardware limitations. Multiprocess Python scripts need a
`if __name__ == "__main__":` guard. Device/precision support must be validated on
your hardware; the package does not select a device or numerical mode for you.

## Prediction and density

| Method | Return and options |
|---|---|
| `predict(inputs, *, conditioning=None, n_samples=None, seed=0, num_steps=50, solver="heun")` | NumPy `(B,T,C)` in original units. For deterministic models, omit `n_samples`; for stochastic models explicitly supply it to request a Monte Carlo mean. |
| `sample(inputs, n_samples=100, seed=0, num_steps=50, solver="heun", *, conditioning=None)` | NumPy `(B,S,T,C)` for stochastic models only. `num_steps` and `solver="heun"` or `"euler"` control flow-matching integration. |
| `log_prob(inputs, outputs)` | iTARFlow only, NumPy `(B,)` continuous trajectory log density including scaling Jacobian and Gaussian constants. |
| `log_prob_tensor(inputs, outputs)` | iTARFlow only, PyTorch `(B,)`, preserving gradients through original-unit tensors `(B,P)` and `(B,T,C)`. |

`inputs` accepts a named mapping, a table with matching named columns, or an
array `(B,P)` in fitted order. A mapping of scalars requests one setting. Named
schemas reject missing/extra columns. Input range warnings flag extrapolation,
not all poorly covered joint combinations. Predictions are not clipped.

For conditioned models, supply a finite original-unit array `(B,T,K)` in
`observed_outputs` order. It is required for every call; unconditioned models
reject it. Transformer conditions on prior observed history, while flow matching
uses the whole supplied path. See [conditioning](conditioning.qmd).

Generated variability represents the learned simulator distribution, not
uncertainty in neural weights. Density evaluation is not an observation model,
a discrete count probability or a posterior. See the [likelihood exercise](../sbi/vi-mcmc.qmd).

## EvaluationReport

`surrogate.evaluate(bank, n_samples=100, seed=42, num_steps=50, solver="heun",
constraints=None, batch_size=64)` is equivalent to `metis.evaluate(surrogate, bank, ...)`.
The bank must have the full fitted schema and grid, including observed channels.
Evaluation supplies those channels as conditioning and scores predicted channels.
`batch_size` bounds evaluation memory; all runs are evaluated. Stochastic
metrics require at least two samples; changing batch size changes Monte Carlo draws.

The report exposes `metrics` (aggregate dictionary), `by_output` and `by_group`
(Polars tables), and `provenance`. `to_dict()` serializes a report;
`save(path)` writes JSON; `worst_groups(n=10)` ranks group RMSE;
`plot(output=None, max_runs=4)` requires the `[plots]` extra. Metrics include
MAE/RMSE, replicate-mean error when supported, and stochastic empirical CRPS,
pointwise 90% coverage and interval width. See [evaluation](evaluation.qmd)
for metric definitions, partition handling and constraint syntax.

## Persistence and inspection

`surrogate.save(path)` writes a versioned inference artifact;
`Surrogate.load(path, device="cpu")` returns a ready model without the bank.
It includes schemas, times, scalers, weights, resolved architecture, bounds and
training provenance. A training checkpoint instead includes optimizer/RNG state
for strict resume and is configured through `TrainingConfig`. Neither loader
silently reinterprets the other's files. See [saving and loading](../basics/saving-and-loading.qmd).

Inspect `input_names`, `output_names`, `observed_outputs`, `training_output_names`,
`times`, `history`, `training_metadata`, `resolved_model_options`, `model_config`,
`parameter_count` and `is_stochastic`. Fitted `input_scaler`, `output_scaler`,
and optional `conditioning_scaler` contain the means, scales and constant masks.
`model.model` is the underlying PyTorch module for advanced use.

## Other modules

- `load_example()` loads the bundled 100-group, 40-timepoint SIRDS subset.
- `assess_coverage(training, candidates)` reports marginal bounds and distance
  to existing inputs; `suggest_simulations(training, candidates, n=10)` selects
  a geometric coverage design from supplied valid candidates. Neither estimates
  posterior uncertainty or guarantees low surrogate error.
- `Standardizer.fit(array, axis=0)` uses population standard deviation;
  `transform` and `inverse_transform` preserve units across scaling. Constant
  dimensions have scale one and a recorded mask. New fits use float64 scaling
  arithmetic before the float32 network.
- `metis.preprocessing.truncate_simulations(bank, start_time=...)` and
  `initialize_static_inputs(bank, mapping={"initial_stock": "stock"})` are
  explicit opt-in transformations, preserving scenario/replicate identities.
- `metis.tracking.WandbTracker` is a context manager; pass
  `on_progress=tracker.log_training`, then `tracker.log_evaluation(report, prefix="test")`.
  It logs supplied configuration and scalar metrics, optionally offline.
- `metis.migration.LegacyPreprocessing` and `import_legacy_checkpoint` provide
  a strict, inference-only import of supported historical static models when
  their exact preprocessing is supplied. See [migration](migration.qmd).
